title: Atomic Structure and Orbitals

cards.b: Sodium explodes in water; neon does nothing. Both are made of protons, neutrons and electrons. The difference lies in how electrons are arranged. Electron arrangement decides almost all of chemistry: colour, bonding, reactivity, even why lasers work.

Niels Bohr, 1913, proposed that electrons orbit the nucleus only in fixed energy levels (shells). An electron can jump up by absorbing exact energy, and falls down by releasing it as light.

That explained why hydrogen glows in specific colours only: each colour is one jump. Shells hold at most 2n^2 electrons: 2, 8, 18 for n = 1, 2, 3.

Bohr's orbits were too simple. In the 1920s, de Broglie (1924) said electrons behave like waves, Schrödinger (1926) wrote the wave equation, and Heisenberg (1927) showed we cannot know both position and speed exactly.

So we speak of orbitals: regions where an electron is most likely found, not tracks.

• s: spherical. 1 orbital, holds 2 electrons.
  • p: dumbbell. 3 orbitals, holds 6.
  • d: clover. 5 orbitals, holds 10.
  • f: complex. 7 orbitals, holds 14.

Each orbital holds at most 2 electrons with opposite spin. Shell 1 has only 1s; shell 2 has 2s and 2p; shell 3 has 3s, 3p, 3d.

• Aufbau: fill the lowest energy first: 1s, 2s, 2p, 3s, 3p, 4s, 3d, 4p.
  • Pauli exclusion (1925): no two electrons share all four quantum numbers, so an orbital holds max 2.
  • Hund's rule: in a set of equal orbitals, spread electrons singly first, like passengers taking empty bus seats before doubling up.

Count electrons, fill in order.

  • Hydrogen (1): 1s1
  • Carbon (6): 1s2 2s2 2p2
  • Sodium (11): 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s1
  • Neon (10): 1s2 2s2 2p6, a full outer shell

Sodium has one lonely outer electron, easily lost. Neon's outer shell is full, so it is content and inert. That is the whole story of their different behaviour.

Chlorine has 17 electrons.

  1. 1s2 uses 2 (15 left).
  2. 2s2 2p6 uses 8 (7 left).
  3. 3s2 3p5 uses 7 (0 left).

Configuration: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p5. Outer shell has 7 electrons, one short of full, so chlorine grabs an electron to become Cl-. It also becomes isoelectronic with argon (18 electrons).

• Electrons do not orbit like planets. Orbitals are probability clouds.
  • An orbital is not the same as an orbit.
  • 4s fills before 3d, because it is slightly lower in energy for neutral atoms.
  • Light from atoms is not random. Each colour corresponds to a precise energy jump.

Satyendra Nath Bose (1924) developed the statistics of light particles, later extended by Einstein into Bose-Einstein statistics. The particle class boson carries his name.

C.V. Raman discovered in 1928 that light scattered by molecules changes colour slightly, revealing molecular energy levels. The Raman effect won him the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics, and Raman spectroscopy is now a standard chemistry tool.

• Electrons occupy quantised energy levels and orbitals (s, p, d, f).
  • Shell capacity is 2n^2; s, p, d, f hold 2, 6, 10, 14.
  • Fill by Aufbau, Pauli and Hund.
  • Outer electrons decide chemical behaviour.
